question: Conditional on an accepted initial monocular route tangent that lies in frozen NavDP's clipped rear half-plane, does one proof-bound bounded yaw alignment recover controller support without destroying previously successful route-tangent rollouts?
selection_rule: all nine formal mono_cec_route_tangent histories whose terminal partition was not geometry_stream_failure: five stuck failures and four successes
sole_intervention: after the first accepted rear route tangent, discard the pre-turn horizon, execute zero-translation yaw atoms of at most 30 degrees with one fresh RGB observation per atom, update the existing route compass from issued-action receipts, and replan
alignment_authority: accepted CEC certificate plus proof-bound monocular route-tangent packet
baseline: identical certified monocular route tangent with alignment disabled
success_contract: three-dimensional Euclidean distance strictly below 1.0 m
pairing_contract: both arms run in one process and share the exact frozen causal RGB history, query, goal, initial proof, initial route packet, seeds, budget, policy and GPU

decision_rule.advance_to_fresh_confirmation: all execution audits pass, paired aligned-versus-unaligned gains are at least 2, paired losses are at most 1, and net gain is positive
decision_rule.otherwise: do not promote rear alignment into the long-range method

scope_boundary: This test isolates the controller-support layer only. It cannot establish a long-range navigation result and cannot repair the fourteen parent geometry-stream failures by construction.
